title: #release-payments — v2.5 settlement date
body:
Maya Chen: Heads up, v2.5 is going to slip. We hit something in staging we won't ship around.
Arjun Rao: How long?
Maya Chen: Looking like ~2 weeks past the original target. It's tracked in LED-412 — the settlement path can post twice on retry. PAY-501 is blocked on it.
Lena Fischer: Working the fix now, will verify in staging before we call it done.
Maya Chen: Once it's verified we cut the release. Not before.
author: Maya Chen

title: #incidents — duplicate charges in prod (Jun 3)
body:
Maya Chen: Declaring an incident — customers reporting double charges in the last hour.
Arjun Rao: Risk scoring has been timing out under load, payment path retries on timeout (that's RISK-220). Lines up with the spike.
Maya Chen: Retries shouldn't double-charge though. What changed recently on our side?
Arjun Rao: Let me check what landed on the settlement path lately.
Maya Chen: Please do — opening PAY-530 to track the RCA.
author: Maya Chen

title: #incidents — duplicate notifications (Jun 9)
body:
Tom Nguyen: Incident — customers getting duplicate receipts since this morning.
Hana Kim: The bus is at-least-once (ADR-003), so redelivery is normal — the consumer is supposed to dedup those.
Tom Nguyen: Right, so why are dupes getting through now? Did something change in the consumer?
Hana Kim: There was a consumer refactor recently. Let me look at what it touched.
Tom Nguyen: Opening NOT-310 for the RCA.
author: Tom Nguyen

title: #release-notifications — batching status
body:
Hana Kim: Batching (NOT-300) is slipping. After the Jun 9 incident we all moved onto the dedup fix (NOT-320).
Tom Nguyen: Agreed, dedup takes priority. Batching resumes once NOT-320 is out.
Hana Kim: So the batching release is behind purely because of the reprioritization, not because the feature is stuck.
author: Hana Kim

title: #arch — async vs synchronous settlement
body:
Raj Patel: Proposal: move settlement off the request path to async. Synchronous writes are capping our throughput and adding latency to every charge.
Maya Chen: The synchronous approach is simpler and strongly consistent though. What do we give up?
Raj Patel: We accept an eventual-consistency window between charge and ledger entry. The win is throughput and lower payment latency.
Maya Chen: The risk is double-posting if settlement retries.
Raj Patel: Yes — we pair this with idempotency keys so retries are safe. That's a hard requirement, not optional.
Maya Chen: OK, async + idempotency keys it is.
author: Raj Patel

title: #eng-announce — Risk Engine ownership
body:
Maya Chen: Announcement — Risk Engine is moving from Team Pay to the new Team Sentinel, led by Sofia. Tracked in OWN-100.
Sofia Alvarez: Excited to take this on. Team Pay keeps the payment-side scoring client integration; everything else in Risk Engine is ours now.
Maya Chen: Ownership matrix will be updated to reflect Sentinel as the owner.
author: Maya Chen

title: #planning — Q3 milestones and blockers
body:
Sofia Alvarez: For Q3, fraud-scoring v2 (RISK-240) can't start until the Ledger historical export (LED-430) is ready — flagging it as a hard dependency.
Raj Patel: Reconciliation (LED-450) is stuck too, but for a different reason — nobody owns the Payment<->Ledger boundary, so we can't place the logic.
Tom Nguyen: Batching (NOT-300) is the only one of mine in motion.
Sofia Alvarez: Let's make sure the roadmap shows those depends-on links clearly.
author: Sofia Alvarez

title: #team-sentinel — standup
body:
Sofia Alvarez: Standup — fraud-scoring v2 is still blocked. We're idle on it until Team Books delivers the historical export (LED-430). Nothing we can do on RISK-240 until that lands.
Marco Rossi: Confirmed, model training needs that dataset first.
author: Sofia Alvarez

title: #team-books — standup
body:
Raj Patel: Standup — reconciliation (LED-450) is stalled. We have a stub but can't move forward because the ownership of the reconciliation boundary is unresolved. Raising again in #arch.
Lena Fischer: Same blocker as last week then.
author: Raj Patel

title: #arch — who owns Payment<->Ledger reconciliation?
body:
Raj Patel: Who owns the reconciliation boundary between Payment and Ledger? We need an owner to place the LED-450 logic.
Maya Chen: It's not really a payment concern once settlement is handed off — feels like a ledger thing.
Raj Patel: It spans both, though. Books shouldn't unilaterally own a cross-service contract.
Maya Chen: Agreed it's shared, but 'shared' has meant 'nobody' so far. The matrix still says TBD.
Raj Patel: So we're stuck until someone actually claims it.
author: Raj Patel

title: #team-sentinel — debugging scoring timeouts
body:
Marco Rossi: Timeouts on the scoring client spike under load. Adding a retry on timeout so payment auths don't fail (RISK-220).
Sofia Alvarez: Fine, but caution the payment team: a retry means the downstream call can run twice. That's only safe if the caller is idempotent.
Marco Rossi: Good point — as long as their settlement path dedups on retry we're fine.
author: Marco Rossi

title: #team-comms — dedup after the refactor
body:
Hana Kim: Found it — the recent consumer refactor dropped the dedup step. With an at-least-once bus that means every redelivery goes out as a duplicate.
Tom Nguyen: So the refactor removed the one thing protecting us from redelivery. Re-adding dedup under NOT-320.
Hana Kim: Yep. Restoring the event-id dedup.
author: Hana Kim

title: #incidents — payment latency blip (May)
body:
Arjun Rao: Brief latency spike on payments a few minutes ago, p99 climbed then recovered.
Maya Chen: Looks like a cold cache after a node restart — warmed up and back to normal. No failed or duplicated charges.
Arjun Rao: Agreed, self-resolved. No action needed.
author: Arjun Rao

title: #team-sentinel — model v4 rollout
body:
Marco Rossi: Model v4 is rolling out. Canary metrics look good — precision up slightly, latency unchanged.
Sofia Alvarez: Nice. Sign-off to go to 100%?
Marco Rossi: Yes, full rollout. No regressions in scoring behavior.
author: Marco Rossi
